stem: Two source-water samples have nearly the same pH, but one requires substantially more acid to reach the same adjusted pH. Which interpretation is strongest?
choices: The sample needing more acid probably has lower EC, because conductivity controls how quickly pH changes during adjustment
The samples likely differ in alkalinity, so similar starting pH did not describe their acid-neutralizing capacity
The sample needing more acid probably has less dissolved oxygen, which makes its pH harder to move during adjustment
The samples likely differ mainly in temperature, so the warmer source required more acid despite similar starting pH
rationale: Water sources with similar pH can differ in alkalinity. Higher acid-neutralizing capacity can require more acid to produce the same pH change, so pH should not be interpreted alone.
